PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-09
53M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling reasonably well and takes his blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. Family has noticed alternating periods of elevated, high-energy mood with less need for sleep and periods of low mood over recent months, which he is open to exploring. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. He works as a warehouse supervisor. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 196 lb, BMI 29.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema, joints without swelling.
Psych: cooperative, normal speech rate today, linear thought process.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.1%, basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/78. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Concern for bipolar disorder; referred to psychiatry. Provided referral and reviewed warning signs to seek earlier care, including sleep changes and mood escalation.
3. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
4. Family history: reviewed relevant family history and discussed age-appropriate screening and reassurance.

Return in 6 weeks to confirm the psychiatry appointment, sooner as needed.
